steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three high-impact strategies cities can adopt to cut their carbon emissions:

1. Shift how people move  
   • Build out high-quality public transit (bus rapid transit, light rail, metro) so residents can rely less on private cars.  
   • Create safe, continuous walking and cycling networks, complemented by bike-sharing and e-scooter programs.  
   • Encourage electric mobility by installing widespread, convenient charging infrastructure and offering preferential parking or lane access for electric vehicles and shared car fleets.  
   Result: Fewer internal-combustion vehicle miles traveled, less congestion, and lower tailpipe emissions.

2. Retrofit and decarbonize buildings  
   • Tighten energy-efficiency codes for new construction and offer incentives or mandates for deep energy retrofits in existing buildings (insulation, efficient windows, smart controls).  
   • Replace fossil-fuel heating systems with high-efficiency heat pumps or district heating fed by renewables or waste heat.  
   • Deploy rooftop solar, solar water heaters, and green roofs to generate clean power on-site and reduce cooling loads.  
   Result: Buildings—often a city’s largest emissions source—consume less energy and transition away from gas or oil.

3. Clean and localize the urban energy supply  
   • Procure electricity from utility-scale wind, solar, and geothermal projects through power-purchase agreements or municipal utilities.  
   • Encourage distributed generation—rooftop PV, community solar gardens, microgrids—so neighborhoods can produce and store their own zero-carbon power.  
   • Integrate battery storage and smart grid technologies to balance supply and demand, maximizing renewables and minimizing the need for gas peaker plants.  
   Result: The electricity that powers transit, buildings, and industry becomes progressively carbon-free, amplifying the benefits of efficiency and electrification efforts.
